## My request:
wie wird entschieden annn nachfragen gestellt werden?

Aktuell wird das rein deterministisch nach Textlänge entschieden – noch nicht nach inhaltlicher Vollständigkeit:

- 1–34 Zeichen: Nachfrage nach Geschehen und Ort
- 35–69 Zeichen: Nachfrage danach, was künftig unterlassen werden soll
- 70–99 Zeichen: Nachfrage nach Betroffenen und möglichen Wiederholungen
- ab 100 Zeichen: keine Nachfrage, „Generieren“ erscheint

Keine Nachfrage erscheint außerdem, wenn:

- eine PDF hinterlegt wurde oder
- der Text als bestehender Tenor erkannt wird, etwa durch Formulierungen wie „zu unterlassen“, „Ordnungsgeld“ oder „wird verurteilt“.

Das ist momentan eine einfache Demo-Logik. Sinnvoller wäre später eine Prüfung, ob tatsächlich Angaben zu Handlung, Ort/Kanal, Betroffenen und gewünschtem Ergebnis vorhanden sind – unabhängig von der Zeichenanzahl.

+# Interaction contract
+
+Use this reference when implementing input modes, completeness questions, keyboard behavior, searchable records, autocomplete, or proposal selection.
+
+## State model
+
+Model the experience explicitly. Names may vary, but the following states should remain distinguishable:
+
+| State | User-visible behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Empty | instructional placeholder, peripheral tools only |
+| Composing | user text, no unnecessary chrome |
+| Incomplete | one inline question for the highest-priority missing fact |
+| Ready | primary action becomes available |
+| Slash menu | filtered mode commands with active row |
+| Record search | filtered records with active row |
+| Autocomplete | one safe ghost continuation with Tab hint |
+| Generating | action shows progress without replacing user text |
+| Comparing | two editable proposals and no composing footer |
+| Adopted | selected proposal returns to an editable writing state |
+| Error | local, actionable explanation; original input preserved |
+
+Keep orthogonal state separate: input text, active mode, selected record, attachment, completeness, command query/index, record query/index, autocomplete, proposal texts, and selected proposal.
+
+## Semantic completeness
+
+Never use character count as the main readiness rule. Define 3–6 domain-specific semantic dimensions. Typical dimensions are:
+
+- object or subject;
+- observed event, desired operation, or concrete task;
+- location, channel, source, or scope;
+- affected audience or target;
+- desired outcome or constraint;
+- known exception or boundary when needed for safety.
+
+The checker should return structured data, not just a boolean:
+
+```ts
+type Completeness = {
+  complete: boolean;
+  missing: string[];
+  nextQuestion: string | null;
+};
+```
+
+Ask only the first high-priority missing question. Questions must name the missing concept and preferably give two or three short examples. Do not ask generic prompts such as “Please provide more context.”
+
+Use deterministic logic when possible. If an AI classifier is required, validate its output and preserve a deterministic fallback. Treat pasted existing output according to its mode; correction may be possible without all facts required for generation from scratch.
+
+## Slash modes
+
+Typing `/` at a valid command boundary opens the mode menu. Match only the current slash token, normally from `/` to the next whitespace. Filtering is case-insensitive and should search command plus human-readable title.
+
+Recommended commands should describe interpretation, not pages. Examples:
+
+- `/describe` — create from a new description;
+- `/revise` — improve an existing draft;
+- `/records` — select prior work or a trusted source.
+
+Use the vocabulary and language of the product. Limit the initial list to modes that materially change behavior.

+Keyboard contract:
+
+| Key | Slash menu behavior |
+|---|---|
+| ArrowDown | select next visible command; wrap at end |
+| ArrowUp | select previous visible command; wrap at start |
+| Enter | adopt selected command; do not insert newline |
+| Escape | close menu while preserving useful text |
+| Pointer hover | synchronize the keyboard index |
+| Pointer click | adopt clicked command |

+Reset the active index to zero whenever the filtered query changes. If there are no results, show a compact empty message and let ordinary typing continue.

+4. Keep the list small, usually five to eight results.

+4. Escape behavior;

+Use this reference when writing code, structuring state, or validating the completed workspace.
+
+## Recommended separation
+
+Keep the primary route thin enough to understand. Extract domain logic into pure functions or services:
+
+```text
+route/page component
+├─ writing surface and menus
+├─ state transitions
+├─ completeness checker (pure)
+├─ mode/record search (pure)
+├─ autocomplete source (pure or service)
+├─ proposal builder/client
+└─ provenance and approval model
+```

+Avoid one generic “AI response” state. Proposal content, source IDs, warnings, and selection are separate values with separate lifecycle rules.

+
+Adapt this model rather than copying it verbatim:
+
+```ts
+type WorkspaceState<Mode, Record, Proposal> = {
+  text: string;
+  mode: Mode | null;
+  selectedRecord: Record | null;
+  attachment: { name: string; status: "selected" | "processing" | "ready" | "failed" } | null;
+  completeness: {
+    complete: boolean;
+    missing: string[];
+    nextQuestion: string | null;
+  };
+  commandMenu: { open: boolean; query: string; index: number };
+  recordMenu: { open: boolean; query: string; index: number };
+  autocomplete: { text: string; sourceId?: string } | null;
+  generation: "idle" | "running" | "failed";
+  proposals: [Proposal, Proposal] | null;
+  selectedProposal: 0 | 1 | null;
+};

+  outcome: hasDesiredOutcome(input),

+const nextQuestion = !checks.subject
